title: Guardrails as Code (GaC)
oneliner: Put your AI policies and governance rules into the CI/CD pipeline as code, so every agent project is checked against them from start to finish automatically.
says: Guardrails as Code is becoming popular in AI agent projects. Guardrails matter at every stage - prompting, inferencing, and the agent architecture itself. GaC means encoding your policy and governance details into the CI/CD pipeline, which then enforces those guardrails across the whole AI agent project from beginning to end. He urges you to explore it and implement it in your organization.
explained: The problem this solves: governance as documents does not scale. A policy PDF says what should happen; nothing checks whether it did. GaC moves the policy to where the work flows - the pipeline. Every change to prompts, models, or agent wiring passes through automated checks: Is this model approved? Does this prompt leak instructions? Is PII handling in place? Fail the check, fail the build.

This is the same evolution security went through with DevSecOps - policy moved from annual audits into the pipeline - and he is right that AI is following. Note how it connects to his Season 2 platform: the prompt registry, evaluation platform, and tool catalog are the things the guardrails check against. GaC is the enforcement arm of all of them.
takeaway: Governance that lives in documents gets ignored; governance that lives in the pipeline gets enforced. Encode policies as automated checks in CI/CD.
